signals.title: USD — FOMC Decision + Yield Curve Regime
signals.text: The US Dollar (DXY) tumbles to 100.84 after a divided Federal Reserve hold at 3.50%-3.75%, defying market pricing for a 30% hike probability. The 9-3 vote with significant hawkish dissents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) and Warsh's vow to return inflation to 2% has triggered a Bear Steepener regime, with the 2s10s spread widening to +31.2bp. While nominal rates remain on hold, the US real rate of +1.59% remains the most restrictive in the G10, yet the dollar is failing to hold its SMA20 support at 101.06. This divergence between hawkish verbal guidance and the failed hike delivery is forcing a liquidation of USD length. Implication: USD remains under pressure until the market reconciles the 'resolute' hawkish rhetoric with the actual pause in the hiking cycle. Risk: Resilience in US stocks and a reversal in the VIX from 20.7 sparks a 'higher-for-longer' carry bid that stabilizes DXY above 101.00.

signals.title: EUR/AUD — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: EUR/AUD shows a prominent G10 bilateral theme with a 1.120% spread between the week's strongest and weakest currencies. EUR outperformance (+0.578% avg) comes despite a carry disadvantage of -195bp against the AUD (ECB 2.4% vs RBA 4.35%). The divergence is fundamentally driven by data trends: AUD ESI sits at a strong negative -21.2 (37 misses) while EUR exhibits a milder negative bias at -12.5. EUR/USD at 1.1471 is now testing the SMA50 at 1.1492, whereas AUD/USD remains capped below its own SMA50 of 0.7021. The options market is pricing an elevated vol premium in AUD/USD (VRP +7.5%), suggesting heightened hedging demand as the RBA hike bias fails to support the currency against data disappointments. Risk: RBA delivers a hawkish surprise on 11 Aug, closing the ESI gap and reviving the AUD carry advantage.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry + Options Skew + Geopolitical
signals.text: USD/JPY at 163.45 remains bid by a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential, though WTI oil surging +6.72% on Middle East escalation introduces significant JPY intervention risk. COT LF net positioning remains heavily short JPY at -114,030, leaving the pair vulnerable to a disorderly unwind if volatility spikes further. The options market reflects this tail risk with a strong USD/JPY 25d RR put skew of -1.55, indicating that institutions are paying up for downside protection despite the spot price holding above the SMA20 (162.57). JPY ESI at +17.2 supports a stronger JPY on a data basis, contradicting the carry-driven short. Implication: The carry trade is in a high-fragility state where any VIX move above 25 likely triggers a rapid retreat toward the 161.24 SMA50 level. Risk: VIX remains below 25 and the BoJ hold on 31 Jul validates the existing carry crowdedness.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Volatility Risk Premium + ESI
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8135, having cleared its SMA20 (0.8100) but facing extreme pricing in the options market. The pair exhibits a massive Volatility Risk Premium (VRP) of +12.4%, with IV at 18.6% dwarfing the realized HV30 of 6.2%. This suggests the market is pricing in a volatility shock that has yet to manifest in spot price action, likely tied to safe-haven demand given the Middle East headlines. CHF ESI at +26.1 (16 beats) indicates the currency is supported by superior fundamental data compared to the USD's neutral -2.1. Retail sentiment is 67% short USD/CHF, aligning with the institutional put skew. Implication: Elevated VRP and strong CHF data bias suggest the pair is prone to a sharp mean-reversion lower if the 'divided' Fed narrative continues to weaken the dollar. Risk: A sustained bear steepener in the US curve keeps the 375bp nominal carry advantage attractive enough to offset CHF's data strength.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5797 is testing its SMA50 resistance at 0.5793, supported by an accommodative real rate of -1.56% and a strong positive ESI of +24.7. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. This positioning extreme (bottom 20% of long range) suggests significant short-squeeze potential if upcoming NZ data continues to beat expectations. The pair has already gained 2.77% over the last month, yet specs have failed to cover. Implication: A close above the SMA50/SMA200 cluster (0.5793-0.5825) would likely force a technical capitulation of the spec short. Risk: RBNZ pivots to a hold stance in response to global tightening, validating the current spec short position.
